chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Jamil and Hisham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The proof is upon the one who claims, and the oath is upon the one who is claimed against.'

key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: The proof or evidence presented by the claimant
key_terms.الْيَمِينُ: The oath taken by the defendant to confirm their denial
key_terms.مَنِ ادَّعَى: The one who makes the claim
key_terms.مَنِ ادُّعِيَ عَلَيْهِ: The one against whom the claim is made

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal principle regarding the burden of proof and oaths in court?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Kulayni, articulates the legal maxim 'al-bayyinah 'ala al-mudda'i' which serves as a cornerstone of Shia jurisprudence for resolving civil disputes. It establishes that the initial burden of proof rests on the claimant, while the defendant may clear themselves via a solemn oath, a principle deeply rooted in the Prophetic tradition and elaborated upon by scholars like al-Shaykh al-Mufid and al-Tusi in their works on usul al-fiqh.
